items.text: Produce some water waves using the vibrator.
Measure the distance between successive crests in the deeper part, \(\lambda\) and then in the shallow part, \(\lambda_1\).
What is the relationship between the ratio of wave velocities in the deep and shallow parts of the tank?

elements.text: When water waves travel from a deep part to a shallow part, the wavelength decreases as illustrated in Figure 1.18. However, the frequency of the waves does not change. Since velocity, v, is given by \(f\lambda\), the velocity of the waves decreases with decrease in wavelength.

elements.text: **Figure 1.18:** Change in the wavelength of water waves
The ratio \(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_1}\) is equal to the ratio of the velocities of water waves in the deep water, v to that in the shallow water, \(v_1\)
The velocity of water waves is higher in the deep water than in the shallow water.

The refraction of water waves can be further observed if the boundary between the deep and shallow regions is at a certain angle to the incident wavefronts. In this case the deep region acts as the first medium while the shallow region acts as the second medium. If in Activity 1.2, the glass plate was placed at some angle, water waves would be refracted as shown in Figure 1.19.
